chunks: From him, from his father, raising it (to the Prophet or Imam), said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The deceased is questioned in his grave about five things: about his prayer, his alms-tax, his pilgrimage, his fasting, and his Wilayah (guardianship) of us, the People of the Household. So Wilayah says to the other four from the side of the grave: 'Whatever enters among you that is deficient, I am upon it to complete it.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the Household (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the five things a deceased person is questioned about in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies five pillars of accountability in the grave, uniquely elevating Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt to the same status as the primary acts of worship. The phrase ' Wilayah is from the side of the grave' signifies that this spiritual bond is intrinsic to the soul's identity in Barzakh, serving as a divine compensatory mechanism that rectifies any deficiencies in prayer, fasting, zakat, and Hajj. This underscores the Shia theological view that correct belief in the Imams is not merely supplementary but essential for the perfection of one's ritual obligations.
